subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should scheduled cron agentTurn sessions get a first-class hard tool policy such as `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny`, and where should it sit relative to per-job `toolsAllow` and existing subagent/sandbox policy layers?
rationale: This would add a public config surface and a scheduled-execution security boundary; choosing inheritance or precedence incorrectly could either leave cron overpowered or break existing jobs that rely on current tool exposure.

options.title: Add first-class cron policy
options.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` as a distinct cron layer, define deny/allow precedence against per-job `toolsAllow`, and document upgrade-safe behavior.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Treat cron sessions as sharing `tools.subagents.tools` to avoid a new config block, accepting that subagent and scheduled-job semantics become coupled.

options.title: Keep per-job allowlists only
options.body: Leave `--tools` and payload `toolsAllow` as the supported boundary and close or narrow this request to docs and safer defaults.

recommendation.title: Add first-class cron policy
recommendation.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` as a distinct cron layer, define deny/allow precedence against per-job `toolsAllow`, and document upgrade-safe behavior.
